issues.t: Automatic transmission overheats, slips or fails
issues.sym: Harsh or late shifts, slipping, a transmission overheat warning, a burning smell or smoke, or the truck refusing to move in gear.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic is the most-reported failure on these trucks in NHTSA owner complaints. Heat is the main enemy, especially when towing, climbing or driving in four-wheel-drive low.
issues.next: If the overheat light comes on, pull over and let it idle to cool. Check the fluid level and smell. Old, burnt fluid or slipping needs a transmission shop's diagnosis before it gets worse.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt loosens and pulley comes off
issues.sym: A wobble or knocking at the front of the engine, then a sudden loss of power steering and charging. In bad cases the belts and pulley fall off and the engine quits.
issues.why: The bolt that holds the crankshaft pulley on the V6 can lose its tightness over time. Once it backs out, the pulley that drives the power steering pump and alternator works loose.
issues.next: If you hear a knock at the front of the engine or the steering suddenly goes heavy, stop driving. Have a shop check the pulley and bolt; catching it early can save the crankshaft.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley bolt may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before failure. If the pulley comes loose you lose power steering assist, which makes the truck hard to steer.
issues.why: Mitsubishi found the crankshaft pulley bolt on the 3.0L V6 could loosen and let the pulley fall off (NHTSA campaign 00V311).
issues.next: Run the VIN on NHTSA's recall site or call a Mitsubishi dealer to see if the free bolt re-torque was done.

issues.t: Frame and subframe rust-through
issues.sym: Heavy flaking rust under the truck, holes in the frame rails, the truck pulling or wandering, or a failed safety inspection.
issues.why: Owners in salt-belt states report frames and the rear subframe rotting through, sometimes with cracks. Road salt collects in the frame and rusts it from the inside.
issues.next: Have the frame inspected on a lift, tapping suspect spots with a hammer. Serious frame rot is a safety problem; ask the shop whether the frame can be safely repaired.

issues.t: Horn sounds by itself
issues.sym: The horn blasts on its own while driving or parked, often in cold weather, and may not stop until the fuse is pulled.
issues.why: This is one of the most common owner complaints on 2001-2003 trucks. The fault is in the horn circuit, usually the horn switch contacts in the steering wheel pad or the horn relay.
issues.next: Pull the horn fuse or relay to silence it, then have the horn switch and relay tested. Remember the horn won't work until it's fixed.

issues.t: Front brakes wear fast and rotors warp
issues.sym: A pulsing brake pedal or shaking steering wheel when stopping, squealing or grinding, and pads that need replacing well before 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Many owners report short pad life and warped front rotors on these trucks. The brakes work hard on a heavy SUV and heat builds up in the rotors.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors measured. Replace rotors in pairs with quality parts, and check that the caliper slides move freely.

issues.t: Worn tie rods and loose steering
issues.sym: The truck wanders or pulls, the steering feels loose, the wheel shimmies, or the front tires wear unevenly. A tie rod that separates can cause a sudden loss of steering.
issues.why: Front steering and suspension parts such as tie rod ends and the pitman arm wear with age and mileage. RepairPal lists worn front steering parts as a common problem for this SUV.
issues.next: Have the front end checked for play, then replace worn parts and get an alignment. Don't ignore clunks or wandering.

issues.t: Fuel leak from the tank after filling up
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell or gas dripping under the rear of the truck, especially right after filling the tank or when parked on a slope.
issues.why: Owners report fuel seeping from the tank area, often after a full fill-up. Age and rust around the tank, its seals and the filler connections are the usual causes.
issues.next: Don't drive or park in a garage with a fuel leak. Have the tank, filler neck and hoses inspected right away.

issues.t: Oil leaks and burning oil smell
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, oil spots under the truck, oil on the spark plug wires, or the engine using oil between changes.
issues.why: Camshaft and valve cover seals harden with age and leak oil onto hot engine parts. Some high-mileage engines also burn oil, and a few owners report oil sludge from skipped oil changes.
issues.next: Find where the oil is coming from and fix the seals or gaskets. Keep up with oil changes and check the level often.

issues.t: Coolant leaks and overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbing or behaving oddly, coolant puddles, a sweet smell, or steam from under the hood.
issues.why: Owners report burst coolant hoses, failed water pumps and, in some cases, head gasket leaks. Overheating a V6 can quickly damage the engine.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Have the cooling system pressure-tested. If the water pump goes, it is usually replaced with the timing belt.

issues.t: Alternator failure and dead battery
issues.sym: Battery light on, dim lights, a dead battery, or the alternator overcharging and blowing fuses.
issues.why: Several owners report repeated alternator failures, sometimes several in a row, and battery damage from overcharging.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested. Use a quality alternator and check the wiring and belt when replacing it.

issues.t: Catalytic converter or oxygen sensor failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, poor fuel economy, hesitation, a rotten-egg smell, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: High-mileage engines often fail oxygen sensors and catalytic converters. Burning oil or misfires speed up converter damage.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Fix any misfire or oil burning first so a new converter doesn't fail too.

issues.t: A/C compressor failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, or there is a grinding or squealing noise when it turns on.
issues.why: Owners report A/C compressor failures, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the A/C system checked for leaks and compressor clutch operation before replacing parts.

issues.t: Windshield wiper motor stops working
issues.sym: The wipers stop working, work only some of the time, or stall partway across the glass.
issues.why: Owners report wiper motor burnout, especially after the wipers were frozen to the glass. A loose wiper linkage can cause the same symptom.
issues.next: Free iced wipers before turning them on. Have the motor and linkage checked; driving in rain without wipers is dangerous.

issues.t: Engine knock on California-market trucks
issues.sym: A knocking sound from the engine.
issues.why: Consumer Guide reports engine knock on some early California-market trucks, possibly from welding flash getting into the cylinders.
issues.next: Have the engine diagnosed. A knock that gets louder needs attention before it turns into engine damage.

issues.t: Valve tapping for a few minutes after cold start
issues.sym: A light ticking from the top of the engine for a minute or two after a cold start, then it goes away.
issues.why: Consumer Guide notes this short-lived valve tapping is considered normal for these years.
issues.next: No repair needed if it fades quickly. If it stays or gets louder, check the oil level and have it looked at.

issues.t: Shudder in tight, low-speed turns
issues.sym: A shudder or chatter from the rear when making slow, tight turns like in parking lots.
issues.why: The limited-slip rear differential can chatter in tight turns. Consumer Guide notes a limited-slip additive in the differential oil may fix it.
issues.next: Have the rear differential oil changed with the correct limited-slip additive.

issues.t: Radio noise when the power seat moves
issues.sym: Static or noise through the speakers when adjusting the power seat.
issues.why: A wiring issue in the power seat harness; Consumer Guide says a revised harness fixes it.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or shop about the revised power seat wiring harness.

issues.t: Brake vacuum hose can burst (recall)
issues.sym: A hard brake pedal and longer stopping distances if the hose fails.
issues.why: The brake booster vacuum hose on 3.5L trucks did not meet the federal brake hose standard and could burst (NHTSA campaign 01V027).
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. If the pedal feels hard, have the vacuum hose and booster checked right away.

issues.t: Transmission fluid can vent onto the exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell after driving fast in four-wheel-drive low range.
issues.why: On 4WD automatics, too much heat in the transmission could push fluid out the vent onto the hot exhaust, which could catch fire (NHTSA campaign 99V041).
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall. The fix limits speed in 4WD low to about 30 mph and moves the breather vent.

issues.t: Tire and loading label lists wrong weights (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The door label shows the wrong load capacity, so you could overload the truck without knowing it.
issues.why: The tire and loading information label printed incorrect capacity weights (NHTSA campaign 04V095).
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer for the corrected label, and don't load the truck beyond its rated capacity.
